chunks: Whatever was in it from Muḥammad ibn Ḥumrān and Jamīl ibn Darrāj, I have narrated it from my father—may Allah be pleased with him—from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥumrān and Jamīl ibn Darrāj.

key_terms.أَبِي: my father; the author’s immediate source in this chain.
key_terms.جَمِيلِ بْنِ دَرَّاجٍ: one of the two narrators to whom this transmission route leads.
key_terms.رَوَيْتُهُ: I transmitted it; indicates the author’s direct statement of transmission.
key_terms.سَعْدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: a transmitter named in the sanad/isnad.
key_terms.مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ: a transmitter named in the sanad/isnad.
key_terms.مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حُمْرَانَ: one of the two narrators to whom this transmission route leads.

ai.seo_question: What is the transmission chain for narrations from Muḥammad ibn Ḥumrān and Jamīl ibn Darrāj in Man Lā Yaḥḍuruhu al-Faqīh?
ai.summary: This passage clarifies the sanad/isnad for reports transmitted from Muḥammad ibn Ḥumrān and Jamīl ibn Darrāj in the book. It is a technical chain statement identifying the author’s route of transmission through his father and several named transmitters back to those two narrators.
